newsitem.title: FINLAND: WAGE RESTRAINT COULD BRING TAX CUTS - NIINISTO.
newsitem.headline: WAGE RESTRAINT COULD BRING TAX CUTS - NIINISTO.

text.p: There will be scope for further tax cuts if the budget balance improves as currently projected and if the next incomes settlement is moderate, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto told a seminar on Monday.
"If the budget balance improves as expected and if the next round of income settlement talks finds wage moderation, there will again be scope for additional tax cuts," he said.

Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said in September that the next time a cut in income taxes could come would be in connection with the next income settlement talks, "if there is will to reach a comprehensive all-round agreement".
Next year, income taxes will fall by 5.5 billion markka and the total tax rate will fall 0.5 percentage points to 48 percent.
The next round of income settlement talks is due late next year and agreements are scheduled to start in 1998.
